subject: Conditional residency checklist & tenant scoping for TIA (HealthSync)
messages:
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@healthsync.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@healthsync.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional residency & tenant scoping for our TIA

Hi Laura / Kim,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving toward a pilot that will route some requests to EU-hosted inference but keep a subset of customer tenants strictly onshore (UK). Legal asked us to scope what evidence and architecture changes Redwood needs to support a conditional residency configuration per-tenant during a TIA.

Top asks from HealthSync legal:
- A short checklist of artifacts they can expect (TIAs, SCC mapping, UK addendum mapping, subprocessor list).
- Clear onshore-fallback behavior: if EU capacity is exhausted, what are the contractual and technical options to keep UK tenant data in-country?
- Confirmation of whether Redwood can produce tenant-level routing logs (per-tenant region decision) and the retention window for those logs.

We attached the high-level data flow and our current subprocessor matrix. Can you outline the minimal evidence set and a proposed sequencing for the TIA? Our target is to get legal signoff by month-end.

Appreciate any quick pointers — we can jump on a call if that helps.

Best,
Alex Garcia
Director, Product Ops
HealthSync

--- Attachment: data_flow_map_v2.pdf (diagram, 1.2MB)
--- Attachment: subprocessor_matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@healthsync.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional residency & tenant scoping for our TIA

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments.

Quick summary up front: yes, we can support tenant-level residency controls and produce per-tenant routing logs suitable for a TIA. Below is a pragmatic checklist to get HealthSync from discovery -> TIA evidence handoff. I kept it intentionally short so legal can review quickly.

Redwood minimal evidence & sequencing (proposed):
1) DPA + SCC/UK Addendum mapping doc (high level) — we will provide a one-page mapping that shows where SCCs map to our controls and where the UK IDTA addendum applies.
2) Tenant routing design + data flow diagram (you already started this; we will annotate).
3) Subprocessor roster + access boundaries (CSV) — include which subprocers may touch cached tokens or logs.
4) Technical controls attestation (encryption, egress controls, KMS boundaries).
5) Tenant-level routing logs sample & retention policy — we will provide a 90-day sample and the configuration options (90/180/365).
6) Fallback/runbook for onshore-only tenants — steps and SLA implications.

Notes on onshore fallback (short):
- We can implement a hard pin for a tenant to a UK-only serving path (no EU routing) or configure a prioritized routing that prefers UK and only permits EU if explicit failover is allowed.
- For contractual purposes, the hard pin is the clearest. Prioritized routing requires documented controls and a fallback SLA clause.

Kim and Tessa — can you confirm the technical feasibility and an estimated workback for the annotated data flow + the tenant routing logs sample? Alex, I will aim to produce the DPA/SCC mapping and the attestation template by EOD Thursday if that works.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@healthsync.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional residency & tenant scoping for our TIA

Laura / Alex — technical confirmation below. I left in a few operational caveats.

Feasibility (short):
- Tenant pin to UK-only serving path: doable within our deployment abstraction. Will require a small config surface and a rollout plan to avoid routing drift.
- Prioritized routing (UK preferred, EU fallback): doable but requires explicit logging and a contract clause for allowable failover.

What we will deliver for the TIA evidence packet (engineering):
- Annotated data flow PDF (we will overlay service names and where keys/IVs are held).
- Tenant routing logs sample (we can generate a 90-day slice; format: csv with tenant_id,timestamp,route_decision,reason).
- Subprocessor access notes: which infra teams and third parties can see routing decisions (list of job roles + subprocessor name).

Caveats / operational risks:
- Hard pins eliminate our ability to burst EU capacity for those tenants — that will increase unit costs and may require a contractual SLA note.
- Prioritized routing introduces an availability vector if UK capacity is constrained; we suggest an explicit fallback SLA (e.g., keep attempts local for X minutes before failover).

Workback: annotated data flow + logs sample by Thu EOD (May 20). Implementation config for hard pin will be scoped after TIA signoff (2-3 sprint effort for UI + rollout guardrails).

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Prod Engineer, Serving Runtime
